name: Schrödinger Equation - Time-Dependent
definition: Fundamental equation of quantum mechanics describing how quantum state evolves over time.
formula: iℏ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ where Ĥ is Hamiltonian operator

name: Schrödinger Equation - Time-Independent
definition: Eigenvalue equation for stationary states with definite energy.
formula: Ĥψ = Eψ where E is energy eigenvalue
examples: Particle in a box: Eₙ = n²π²ℏ²/(2mL²)

name: Quantum Operators
definition: Mathematical operators representing physical observables in quantum mechanics.
formula: Position: x̂; Momentum: p̂ = -iℏ∂/∂x; Energy: Ĥ

name: Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
definition: Quantum system with parabolic potential, exactly solvable with discrete energy levels.
formula: V(x) = ½mω²x²; Eₙ = ℏω(n + ½)

name: Quantum Tunneling
definition: Quantum phenomenon where particles penetrate through potential barriers classically forbidden.
formula: Transmission coefficient T ≈ exp(-2κa) where κ = √(2m(V-E))/ℏ

name: Hydrogen Atom
definition: Exactly solvable quantum system of electron in Coulomb potential of proton.
formula: Eₙ = -13.6 eV/n²; ψₙₗₘ described by quantum numbers n,l,m
examples: Ground state: n=1, l=0, E=-13.6 eV

name: Spin and Pauli Matrices
definition: Intrinsic angular momentum of particles; Pauli matrices represent spin-1/2 operators.
formula: Ŝ = (ℏ/2)σ where σ are Pauli matrices; [Sᵢ,Sⱼ] = iℏεᵢⱼₖSₖ

name: Quantum Entanglement
definition: Quantum state of multiple particles that cannot be described independently; correlations persist at distance.

name: Uncertainty Principle
definition: Fundamental limit on precision of simultaneous measurements of conjugate variables.
formula: ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2; ΔEΔt ≥ ℏ/2
examples: Cannot know exact position and momentum simultaneously

name: Quantum States and Wavefunctions
definition: Mathematical description of quantum system; |ψ⟩ in Hilbert space, ψ(x,t) in position representation.
formula: ⟨ψ|ψ⟩ = 1 (normalization); P(x) = |ψ(x)|² (probability density)

name: Boltzmann Distribution
definition: Probability distribution of particles over energy states in thermal equilibrium.
formula: P(E) = (1/Z)exp(-E/kT) where Z is partition function

name: Partition Function
definition: Sum over all states weighted by Boltzmann factor; encodes thermodynamic information.
formula: Z = Σᵢexp(-Eᵢ/kT); F = -kT ln(Z) (Helmholtz free energy)
examples: All thermodynamic quantities derivable from Z

name: Entropy and Microstates
definition: Entropy measures disorder; related to number of accessible microstates.
formula: S = k ln(Ω) where Ω is number of microstates

name: Phase Transitions
definition: Abrupt changes in physical properties as external parameter (like temperature) varies.
formula: First order: discontinuous order parameter; Second order: continuous, diverging susceptibility

name: Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein Statistics
definition: Quantum statistics for indistinguishable particles; fermions obey Pauli exclusion, bosons don't.
formula: FD: n(E) = 1/[exp((E-μ)/kT) + 1]; BE: n(E) = 1/[exp((E-μ)/kT) - 1]

name: Maxwell's Equations - Differential Form
definition: Four fundamental equations unifying electricity and magnetism in local form.
formula: ∇·E = ρ/ε₀; ∇·B = 0; ∇×E = -∂B/∂t; ∇×B = μ₀J + μ₀ε₀∂E/∂t
examples: Gauss: electric charges create diverging E

name: Electromagnetic Waves
definition: Self-propagating oscillations of E and B fields traveling at speed of light.
formula: Wave equation: ∇²E = μ₀ε₀∂²E/∂t²; c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3×10⁸ m/s
examples: Radio, microwaves, visible, X-rays, gamma rays

name: Poynting Vector and EM Energy
definition: Energy flux density of electromagnetic field.
formula: S = (1/μ₀)E×B; Energy density: u = ½(ε₀E² + B²/μ₀)

name: Electromagnetic Potentials
definition: Scalar and vector potentials from which E and B fields are derived.

name: Radiation from Accelerating Charges
definition: Accelerating charges emit electromagnetic radiation.
formula: Larmor formula: P = (q²a²)/(6πε₀c³) for nonrelativistic

name: Waveguides and Cavities
definition: Structures that guide or confine electromagnetic waves.
formula: Cutoff frequency: fc = c/(2a) for rectangular waveguide width a

name: Fluid Continuity Equation
definition: Conservation of mass in fluid flow.
formula: ∂ρ/∂t + ∇·(ρv) = 0; Incompressible: ∇·v = 0

name: Navier-Stokes Equations
definition: Fundamental equations governing fluid motion, expressing Newton's second law for fluids.
formula: ρ(∂v/∂t + v·∇v) = -∇p + μ∇²v + f
examples: Describes weather, ocean currents, aircraft flow
Turbulent flow when Re is large

name: Bernoulli's Equation
definition: Energy conservation for ideal fluid flow along streamline.
formula: p + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant
examples: Venturi effect: faster flow → lower pressure

name: Reynolds Number
definition: Dimensionless number characterizing ratio of inertial to viscous forces.
formula: Re = ρvL/μ = vL/ν where ν is kinematic viscosity

name: Boundary Layers
definition: Thin region near solid surface where viscous effects are significant.
formula: Boundary layer thickness δ ∝ √(νx/U)
examples: Transition to turbulence in boundary layer

name: Lagrangian Mechanics
definition: Reformulation of classical mechanics using energy rather than forces.
formula: L = T - V (Lagrangian); Euler-Lagrange: d/dt(∂L/∂q̇) - ∂L/∂q = 0
examples: Double pendulum easier in Lagrangian formalism

name: Hamiltonian Mechanics
definition: Formulation of mechanics using phase space and canonical coordinates.
formula: H = Σpᵢq̇ᵢ - L; Hamilton's equations: q̇ = ∂H/∂p, ṗ = -∂H/∂q

name: Rigid Body Dynamics
definition: Motion of extended objects with fixed shape.
formula: L = Iω (angular momentum); τ = Iα; Parallel axis: I = Icm + Md²

name: Central Force Motion
definition: Motion under force directed toward/away from fixed point.
formula: F = f(r)r̂; Angular momentum conserved: L = mr²θ̇

name: Normal Modes and Oscillations
definition: Coupled oscillators have special modes where all parts oscillate at same frequency.
formula: Find eigenfrequencies ω from det(K - ω²M) = 0

name: Crystal Structure
definition: Periodic arrangement of atoms in solids forming lattice.
formula: Bravais lattice; Reciprocal lattice for k-space
examples: X-ray diffraction: Bragg's law 2d sin(θ) = nλ

name: Band Theory of Solids
definition: Electronic structure in crystals; energy bands separated by gaps.
formula: Bloch theorem: ψₖ(r) = uₖ(r)e^(ik·r)
examples: Insulators: filled valence band, large gap
Semiconductors: small gap, thermally activated carriers

name: Phonons
definition: Quantized lattice vibrations in solids.
formula: ω(k) dispersion relation; Heat capacity from phonon modes
examples: Debye T³ law for heat capacity at low T

name: Superconductivity
definition: Zero electrical resistance and expulsion of magnetic fields below critical temperature.
formula: BCS theory: Cooper pairs; Critical field Hc

name: Ferromagnetism
definition: Spontaneous magnetization due to aligned magnetic moments.
formula: Curie temperature Tc; Below Tc: spontaneous magnetization

name: Radioactive Decay
definition: Spontaneous transformation of unstable nuclei emitting radiation.
formula: N(t) = N₀e^(-λt); Half-life: t₁/₂ = ln(2)/λ

name: Nuclear Fission
definition: Splitting of heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei, releasing energy.
formula: U-235 + n → fission products + neutrons + ~200 MeV
examples: Binding energy per nucleon drives fission

name: Nuclear Fusion
definition: Combining light nuclei to form heavier nucleus, releasing energy.
formula: D + T → He-4 + n + 17.6 MeV; pp-chain in stars

name: Standard Model Particles
definition: Classification of fundamental particles: quarks, leptons, gauge bosons.
formula: 6 quarks (u,d,c,s,t,b); 6 leptons (e,μ,τ,νₑ,νμ,ντ); gauge bosons (γ,W,Z,g,H)

name: Fundamental Forces
definition: Four fundamental interactions: gravity, electromagnetic, weak, strong.
formula: Mediated by gauge bosons: γ (EM), W/Z (weak), gluons (strong)
examples: Strong force binds quarks in protons
EM much stronger than weak at low energy

name: Compton Scattering
definition: Inelastic scattering of photon by electron, demonstrating particle nature of light.
formula: λ' - λ = (h/mₑc)(1 - cos θ)

name: Photoelectric Effect
definition: Emission of electrons from material when illuminated by light above threshold frequency.
formula: KEmax = hf - φ where φ is work function
examples: No emission below threshold, regardless of intensity

name: Blackbody Radiation
definition: Thermal electromagnetic radiation emitted by body in thermal equilibrium.
formula: Planck: u(f) = (8πhf³/c³)/[exp(hf/kT) - 1]; Stefan-Boltzmann: P = σAT⁴

name: Cyclotron and Synchrotron Motion
definition: Charged particle motion in magnetic field follows circular/helical path.
formula: Cyclotron frequency: ωc = qB/m; Radius: r = mv/(qB)

name: Hall Effect
definition: Voltage developed across conductor with current in magnetic field.
formula: VH = IB/(nqt) where n is charge carrier density

name: Plasma Physics
definition: Fourth state of matter: ionized gas with collective behavior.
formula: Debye length: λD = √(ε₀kT/nq²); Plasma frequency: ωp = √(nq²/ε₀m)

name: Doppler Effect - Relativistic
definition: Frequency shift for light from moving source, including time dilation.
formula: f' = f√[(1-β)/(1+β)] for recession, β = v/c

name: Lorentz Transformation
definition: Coordinate transformation between inertial frames in special relativity.
formula: x' = γ(x - vt); t' = γ(t - vx/c²); γ = 1/√(1-v²/c²)
examples: Leads to time dilation, length contraction

name: Conservation Laws in Particle Physics
definition: Conserved quantities in particle interactions: energy, momentum, charge, baryon number, lepton number.
formula: Energy-momentum: E² = (pc)² + (mc²)²
examples: Baryon number: proton cannot decay to lighter particles only
CPT theorem in quantum field theory

name: Feynman Diagrams
definition: Pictorial representation of particle interactions in quantum field theory.
formula: Vertices represent interactions; Lines represent particle propagators
